title: Supplement to the fourth, fifth and sixth editions of the Encyclopaedia Britannica - Volume 1 - EB.14
text: below it, called the _extterior conchoid_. The conchoid being described, will, by its interaction with the occurrence of the circle, give the point E, and consequently the position of trisecting line AD. But such a complex curve must cut the circumference in more points than one, and consequently the problem of angular friction, viewed in its generality, admits to several answers. In fact, there are always three distinct positions of the infected line CE, which will fulfill the conditions of the problem.
